fields.meta_title: Customer Satisfaction Survey: Free CSAT Template | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a customer satisfaction survey that asks the right question at the right moment and alerts an owner on every low rating. Free to start.
fields.hero_description: Build a customer satisfaction survey that asks for a rating after each order or ticket and sends every low score to an owner.
fields.features_heading: Everything a Customer Satisfaction Survey Needs
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the rating, a follow-up for each score and the alert to an owner, and saves every answer in a database you own.
fields.feature_1:
A rating scale that fits the moment

Ask for a 1-5 rating, five stars or a row of faces, then one open question about the reason. Change the scale or the wording later by describing the change in a sentence.
fields.feature_2:
Every response tied to the customer

Pass the customer ID, account, plan, or ticket ID with the survey link and every response is saved with that context. A low CSAT score becomes an account your team can call today.
fields.feature_3:
Follow-up questions that change by score

Happy customers are asked to leave a review others can read, and unhappy ones get a box to explain what went wrong. You set the score that splits them in one line of the prompt.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts on low scores

Send a Slack message to the support lead, a HubSpot task to the account owner, or an email to whoever owns the order. Each alert carries the score, the comment, and the customer.
fields.feature_5:
A CSAT trend you can split

The dashboard is generated with the survey and reads from the same response table. Filter it by agent or week, and share one live view with your team instead of a monthly report.
fields.feature_6:
Responses in a database you own

Every response lands in a table in your project, with no response cap. On paid plans, the full code of the survey and its dashboard exports to your own GitHub repository.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your CSAT Survey With Emergent?

fields.usecase_heading: Satisfaction Surveys Built From One Prompt
fields.tab_content_1:
Spot a slipping account long before renewal

New accounts rate their experience out of 5 on day 7, day 30, and day 90, with one open follow-up each time. Answers are saved with the plan and the customer success manager who owns the account. When a score drops to 2, the CSM gets the comment in Slack next to the earlier scores.
fields.tab_content_2:
Reviews from 5-star buyers, exchanges for low ratings

A week after delivery, the buyer rates the product and the delivery out of five stars and can leave a comment. A 5 on the product sends a link to post a public review. A rating of 2 or lower flags the order for the returns team with the comment and order number attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
Per-account scores in HubSpot before every QBR

Each quarter, every contact at a B2B account rates their product line and can add a comment. Scores roll up by account beside last quarter's, and a short summary lands on the HubSpot company record. When an account's average falls by a point or more, the account executive gets every comment from it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every closed ticket scored, sorted by agent

When a ticket closes, the customer gets a single question on a 1-5 scale about the help they received. Each answer is saved with the agent and with how long the ticket stayed open. A score of 2 or lower posts to the support leads' Slack channel with the comment and a link to the ticket.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Customer Satisfaction Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a customer satisfaction survey: pick the score and the moment, write the follow-ups, route alerts, and read the trend.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Use CSAT when you want a verdict on one transaction, such as a delivery, a closed ticket or a renewal call. How likely a customer is to recommend you is a job for NPS, and ease for CES. Pick one headline score per survey and leave the others for a separate send.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send it close to the experience it rates: on ticket close, seven days after delivery, at day 30 of onboarding, or at quarter end for B2B accounts. Keep the gap short enough that the customer still remembers the details of what happened.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pair the rating with one question about why and one field you will filter by, such as plan or region. Then decide what each end of the scale sees next: a thank-you and a review link at the top, a comment box at the bottom.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tie every response to the customer
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which fields travel with the link before anything goes out: account ID and plan for SaaS, order number for retail, ticket ID for support. Those fields let the dashboard split scores by segment and let every alert name the account behind the number.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a customer satisfaction survey for my customers.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Route low scores to an owner
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who hears about which score before launch. A 1 from a key account might email its owner, while a low ticket rating goes to the support lead in Slack. Name one person per alert and agree how fast they reply to the customer.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Emergent generates the survey with its branching and alerts, plus a CSAT dashboard, all reading from a response database you own. Link it from your app or emails, or publish it on your own domain (included in Emergent, uses credits).
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the CSAT trend each week by segment and product area, and call back every customer who scored 1 or 2 within a day. Tell customers what changed because of their feedback, and adjust the questions and thresholds by prompting as patterns appear.

plan.angle: Searchers want to know what a customer satisfaction survey is, which questions to ask and how CSAT is scored, then want one they can send. Question-list and glossary pages answer the first part and stop. This page owns transactional CSAT: a rating after an order, a support contact or an onboarding milestone, saved with its account, order or ticket, a follow-up that changes with the score, a low score routed to a named owner, and the score's trend by agent, account or week. NPS, effort, whole-journey experience and open feedback belong to the sibling pages and are linked, not covered.
tab_stories: Lumacore rates its onboarding out of 5 at day 7, day 30 and day 90, and when its day 90 score drops to 2 the customer success manager Imani Okafor sees the comment in Slack next to the earlier scores.
A buyer rates running shoes and delivery a week after they arrive; a 5 on the product sends a review link, and a 2-star sizing complaint flags the order for the returns team.

Each quarter every contact at a B2B account rates their product line out of 5, results roll up by account next to last quarter's, and Sundial Bakeries' 1.2-point fall sends every comment to account executive H. Szabo.
A closed ticket triggers a single 1-5 question, scores feed an average per agent for the week, and a 2 on a billing ticket posts to the support leads' channel with a link to the ticket.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Customer Satisfaction Survey That Acts on Every Low Score", hero "Build a customer satisfaction survey that asks for a rating after each order or ticket and sends every low score to an owner." carry the transactional CSAT job; how-to description is one sentence.

intent.evidence: Searchers want the definition, questions, examples and a template: FAQ 1 defines it, FAQ 4 gives the questions ("How satisfied were you with your delivery?"), FAQ 5 an example, FAQ 6 the template, how-to 01-07 the build.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary: "day 7, day 30, and day 90", "Per-account scores in HubSpot before every QBR", "saved with the agent and with how long the ticket stayed open". Interact (quiz specialist) as a table column is a note.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs or full sentences ("Ask for a 1-5 rating", "Pass the customer ID", "Send a Slack message"); tabs open on full sentences ("New accounts rate their experience", "When a ticket closes").

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5 clean; short declaratives ("Pick one headline score per survey and leave the others for a separate send."). Word repetition is a note.

voice.evidence: Operator detail: "A low CSAT score becomes an account your team can call today." Meta description phrasing is a note.

truth.evidence: Send timing and question counts disagree between fields (FAQ 10 "within a day" vs tab 2 "A week after delivery"; FAQ 4 "four or five questions" vs FAQ 10 "under five questions"; mockup b2bQuarterly "five-bullet summary" vs 3 drawn bullets; mockup supportTicket follow-up at "3 or below" vs tab 4 "a single question"); NPS-as-loyalty stated without a quoted source (FAQ 1, how-to 01). Claims prompt-build, api-connect, alerts, database-owned, no-caps, free-start, code-export, custom-domain, realtime are approved; CSAT 1-5 and 4-or-5 share, NPS 0-10 and 9-10 promoters, CES ease are quoted.

distinct.evidence: Owns transactional CSAT; FAQ 8 links customer effort score and FAQ 10 links customer feedback survey (both live) instead of covering them; how-to 01 scopes NPS and CES out.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, no brand, tool-choice or form-filler questions, hub link in item 2, sibling links mid-answer (none ends on a link), each answered first ("A CSAT survey asks customers how satisfied they were...").

images.evidence: Tab 1 alert drawn to #cs-alerts while the copy says "the CSM gets the comment in Slack"; tab 2 prompt "flag the rest" and heading "exchanges for the rest" vs copy "A rating of 2 or lower flags the order". Tabs 3 and 4 match (Sundial Bakeries -1.2 to H. Szabo; ticket #8790 rated 2 to #support-leads).

findings.field: faq item 10; tab_content_2; howto_step_2_des; chip_adds[3]; mockup postPurchase
findings.quote: Send the survey within a day of the experience and keep it under five questions.
findings.issue: The send rule disagrees across fields. FAQ 10 says "within a day of the experience"; tab_content_2 says "A week after delivery"; howto_step_2_des recommends "seven days after delivery, at day 30 of onboarding, or at quarter end"; chip_adds[3] "Add a post-purchase send 7 days after each order is delivered."; mockup postPurchase "sent seven days after delivery". FAQ 3 adds "soon after it happens".
findings.fix: Pick one timing rule and state it everywhere, e.g. FAQ 10: send it as soon as the customer can judge the experience (on ticket close, about a week after delivery), matching step 2 and tab 2.

findings.quote: Keep a short customer satisfaction survey to four or five questions.
findings.issue: FAQ 4 allows four or five questions; FAQ 10 says "keep it under five questions" (four at most). The two answers give different numbers for the same rule.
findings.fix: Use one number in both answers (e.g. five questions or fewer in both).

findings.quote: write a five-bullet summary per account to the HubSpot record
findings.issue: The tab 3 prompt asks for a five-bullet summary; the tab 3 image draws three bullets under "QBR summary in HubSpot". The supportTicket prompt adds "an open follow-up for any score of 3 or below", while tab_content_4 says the customer gets "a single question" and the low-score threshold everywhere else on the tab is 2 ("A score of 2 or lower").
findings.fix: Make the b2bQuarterly prompt say three bullets (or a short summary); make the supportTicket follow-up threshold match tab 4 (a single question, alert at 2 or lower), or add the follow-up to the tab copy at the same threshold.

findings.quote: Related scores measure loyalty and effort instead of satisfaction with a single moment.
findings.issue: That NPS measures loyalty is a statement about a professional standard with no quoted span: the NPS source quote covers only the recommend question and the 0-10 scale. Same claim in howto_step_1_des: "Loyalty over time is a job for NPS, and effort for CES." (effort is sourced; loyalty is not).
findings.fix: Add a domain_sources entry whose quote says NPS measures loyalty (e.g. netpromotersystem.com), or reword both sentences to what is sourced: NPS asks how likely a customer is to recommend you.

findings.quote: When a score drops to 2, the CSM gets the comment in Slack next to the earlier scores.
findings.issue: The copy and the mockup prompt send the alert to one person, the CSM; the image posts it to the shared #cs-alerts channel.
findings.fix: Draw the alert as a Slack direct message to Imani Okafor (no channel), or change the copy to a named channel.

findings.quote: A week after delivery, ask for ratings, request reviews from 5-star buyers, flag the rest
findings.issue: The drawn prompt flags every buyer below 5 and the tab heading "Reviews from happy buyers, exchanges for the rest" promises exchanges to everyone else, but the tab copy flags only "A rating of 2 or lower" (mockup: "flag anything under 3"). Buyers who rate 3 or 4 get nothing in the copy.
findings.fix: Image prompt: "...request reviews from 5-star buyers, flag 2 stars or lower"; heading along the lines of "Reviews from 5-star buyers, exchanges for low ratings".
